CAUSE: `app.merge_test_gate.changed_paths()` returns `None` when Git cannot compute `git diff --name-only <target_sha>...HEAD`. `_prepare_admission_snapshot()` in `app/merge_operations.py` converts that `None` into “cannot derive target-relative merge paths.” The proposed missing-merge-base cause is confirmed as a way to reproduce this exact error: with unrelated histories, triple-dot `git diff` exits 128 with “no merge base,” and `changed_paths()` returns `None`.

The 2,402-path size alone did not reproduce the failure. A scratch repo with 2,402 changed paths, including binary files and renames, returned all paths successfully. The snapshot does not include the refused branch’s repository state, so I could not confirm whether that branch actually lacks a merge base. A failed `git diff` or its 15-second timeout in `_git()` would also produce the same error.

Recommended fix: preserve the underlying Git failure instead of collapsing every error and timeout to `None`, and report the target SHA, worker HEAD, and `git diff` stderr/timeout. Then check whether `git merge-base <target_sha> HEAD` succeeds in the refused branch; if not, repair its history or target ref.
